For automatic metrics, we used BLEU and ChrF.

We used both automatic metrics and human evaluation. We performed our evaluation on a single run for each model. For automatic metrics, we used BLEU  and ChrF . BLEU score focuses on overlap in wordlevel n-grams, whereas ChrF focuses on characterlevel n-grams.

For human evaluation, native speakers of Tigrinya and Amharic and second language speakers of Ge'ez qualitatively looked at 50 random sample predictions... We focused on the following axes when evaluating: (1) rating which translation was better from the given models, (2) identifying words that were mistranslated, and (3) identifying changes in homophones in the translations.

For human evaluation, native speakers of Tigrinya and Amharic and second language speakers of Ge'ez qualitatively looked at 50 random sample predictions, comparing the outputs of the different models.
guideline: rating which translation was better from the given models, (2) identifying words that were mistranslated, and (3) identifying changes in homophones in the translations.
Evaluators rated which translation was better, identified mistranslated words, and noted changes in homophones.

We focused on the following axes when evaluating: (1) rating which translation was better from the given models, (2) identifying words that were mistranslated (e.g, words that were in Amharic for Tigrinya translations and vice versa), and (3) identifying changes in homophones in the translations.
